Organ Function Tests

Kidney, liver and cardiac function tests — what each test measures and what it indicates.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • List kidney, liver and cardiac function tests
  • State normal values of key tests
  • Explain what abnormal results indicate

In simple words

Organ function tests use blood and urine to check how well an organ is working. They help diagnose disease, monitor treatment and assess organ health before surgery.

Common panels: renal (kidney), liver (hepatic) and cardiac function tests.

Kidney function tests

Test Normal value Indicates
Blood urea 15–40 mg/dL Kidney function, protein breakdown
Serum creatinine 0.6–1.2 mg/dL Kidney filtration
Serum uric acid 3–7 mg/dL Purine metabolism, gout risk
Urine output 0.5–1 mL/kg/hour Kidney perfusion

Liver function tests

Test Normal value Indicates
ALT below 40 units/L Liver cell damage
AST below 40 units/L Liver, heart, muscle
Alkaline phosphatase 30–120 units/L Liver, bone
Serum bilirubin 0.3–1.2 mg/dL Liver, bile duct, haemolysis
Serum albumin 3.5–5.0 g/dL Liver synthesis, nutrition

Cardiac markers

Marker Significance
Troponin I/T Myocardial infarction (most specific)
CK-MB Muscle and heart damage
LDH General cell damage

🔴 Creatinine and kidney function

Serum creatinine 0.6–1.2 mg/dL reflects kidney filtration. Rising creatinine suggests worsening kidney function.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Sample collection — collect blood or urine at the right time; label correctly; send promptly.
  • Fasting tests — some tests (glucose, lipids) need fasting; instruct the patient.
  • Monitor trends — a rising creatinine or bilirubin over days matters more than one value.
  • Patient teaching — explain what the test is for and why results take time.
  • Safety — follow standard precautions when collecting samples.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Kidney tests: blood urea, serum creatinine, serum uric acid.
  2. Liver tests: ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin, albumin.
  3. Cardiac markers: troponin (most specific for MI), CK-MB, LDH.
  4. Serum creatinine 0.6–1.2 mg/dL reflects kidney filtration.
  5. Serum bilirubin 0.3–1.2 mg/dL; ALT below 40 units/L.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Blood urea rises in kidney failure and dehydration.
  2. Albumin 3.5–5.0 g/dL reflects liver synthesis and nutrition.
  3. Troponin stays elevated for 7–10 days after MI.
  4. Abnormal results are interpreted with clinical picture, not alone.

📌 Memory trick

Liver panel: “ALT Bili Alb Alk Phos” — ALT, Bilirubin, Albumin, Alkaline phosphatase (+AST).

60-second revision

  • Organ function tests: kidney, liver, heart.
  • Kidney: urea, creatinine, uric acid.
  • Liver: ALT, AST, ALP, bilirubin, albumin.
  • Heart: troponin, CK-MB, LDH.
  • Creatinine 0.6–1.2; bilirubin 0.3–1.2 mg/dL.

Test yourself

Which test best reflects kidney filtration?

Answer: B. Serum creatinine is the best indicator of kidney filtration rate.

The most specific marker for myocardial infarction is:

Answer: C. Troponin I or T is the most specific marker for myocardial infarction.

Serum bilirubin normal range is about:

Answer: A. Normal serum bilirubin is about 0.3–1.2 mg/dL.

ALT below 40 units/L indicates:

Answer: B. ALT within the normal range indicates no significant liver cell damage.

Blood urea rises in:

Answer: A. Blood urea rises when kidney function falls (and in dehydration).
